question: Can a small, labeled selection of protein-language-model attention heads recover residue contacts in one forward pass as accurately as the approximately 19L-pass categorical Jacobian, including on pretraining-aware evaluation data?

key_findings.claim: The proposed readout averages a selected subset of attention-head maps into a one-forward-pass contact score.
key_findings.evidence: Each head map is symmetrized, average-product-corrected, and zero-diagonalized; heads are ranked by mean P@L/2 on a disjoint labeled selection set, and the top-K maps are averaged without fitted head weights. The primary cross-model operating point fixes K=10, while per-architecture sweet-K analyses use a separate sweep.

key_findings.claim: The description 'no per-pair labels' is semantically misleading even though no per-pair regression coefficients are fitted.
key_findings.evidence: Contact labels for every eligible residue pair in each selection protein are used to compute each head's P@L/2 and to select K; the method is label-supervised at the head-selection level.

key_findings.claim: The primary CAMEO-PTA25 split is substantially more pretraining-aware than the inherited Zhang benchmark but is a model-relative proxy rather than a proof of zero contamination.
key_findings.evidence: Starting from 553 post-September-2022 CAMEO targets, a current-UniRef50 filter at 50% identity over at least 80% query coverage leaves 56, of which 39 meet L>=75; 10 are used for selection and 29 for evaluation. The appendix notes that the current release substitutes for ESM-2's 2021_04 release and that cleanliness varies by model.

key_findings.claim: On the leakage-filtered ESM-2-650M evaluation, attention fusion improves materially over both the categorical Jacobian and the globally selected top-1 head.
key_findings.evidence: For N=29 proteins, reported P@L/2 is 0.459 for fusion, 0.369 for logit-CJ, and 0.396 for the globally selected top-1 head; Table 2 inconsistently labels the latter 'per-protein top-1.' The paired bootstrap for fusion versus CJ is reported below 0.001, subject to the test-construction audit below.

key_findings.claim: The leakage-clean within-model margin reproduces across several bidirectional protein language models, but absolute cleanliness is not uniform across all models.
key_findings.evidence: ESM-2-3B, ProtT5-XL, and ESM-1b show correlated fusion gains of about 5.9-9.4 percentage points on the same 29-protein protocol; AMPLIFY and ESM Cambrian pretraining postdates the evaluation cutoff, so their absolute results are marked only partially clean.

key_findings.claim: Representation-CJ extends the categorical-Jacobian construction beyond masked-language-model logits and closely tracks logit-CJ where both are defined.
key_findings.evidence: It measures last-hidden-state displacement under amino-acid substitutions and obtains per-protein and pair-level correlations around 0.95 with logit-CJ across comparable bidirectional models.

anchors.section: K and Table A9, pair-level agreement

key_findings.claim: The appendix numbers contradict the claimed concentrated-head rule that diffuseness predicts sweet-K on every architecture except ESM-2-3B.
key_findings.evidence: Table A7 gives win rates 0.82/0.83/0.70 for ESM-2-35M/150M and ProGen2-xlarge, all above the paper's >=0.65 'concentrated' threshold. Yet Figure A1 peaks at K=7 for 35M and K=20 for ProGen2, while Table A3 peaks at K=20 for 150M. Figure A2 then labels ProGen2 as peaking at K<=3, directly conflicting with Figure A1's K*=20. ESM-2-3B is not the only exception.

anchors.section: Figure A1 and I, head-precision rank distributions

key_findings.claim: The paper's strongest diffuseness-to-K evidence is post-hoc on the evaluation set rather than a fully reported held-out model-selection test.
key_findings.evidence: Table A6 says per-architecture sweet-K is chosen on the Zhang eval-200 K-sweep, and Table A7 computes the diffuseness win rate on the same N=200 evaluation proteins, despite Section 4.4 describing it as a selection-set statistic. Appendix O says a disjoint holdout-K transfer gave nonnegative changes but omits the values; Appendix P validates top-10 ranking stability only for ESM-2-650M, not the cross-architecture K rule.

key_findings.claim: Both attention fusion and representation-CJ largely fail on the two tested causal ProGen2 models.
key_findings.evidence: For ProGen2-xlarge on Zhang eval-200, top-head/repr-CJ/fusion are 0.193/0.056/0.112; for ProGen2-large on Zhang-50 they are 0.033/0.013/0.023. These same-family, different-evaluation results support an association but do not isolate causal masking from scale, corpus, architecture, or dataset.

key_findings.claim: The reported 150x-1600x advantage is a well-specified paired inference-time measurement, but it is not an end-to-end or universally amortized deployment ratio.
key_findings.evidence: On matched A100-80GB bf16 runs and the same proteins, median CJ/fusion times are 4.7/0.032 s (35M), 12.5/0.046 s (150M), 30.1/0.050 s (650M), and 87.3/0.054 s (3B), for 150x-1626x. The one-time labeled head probe is reported only as about 10 forwards, and label acquisition, K/operator search, preprocessing, and multi-query amortization are outside the paired per-protein timing.

anchors.section: O and Table A12, per-test wall-clock

key_findings.claim: The 30-36 percentage-point drop from the Zhang split to CAMEO is an upper bound on overlap-associated benchmark inflation, not a causal estimate of memorization.
key_findings.evidence: The datasets also differ in target difficulty, lengths, contact definitions, temporal coverage, and sampling. The authors themselves describe the comparison as an upper bound rather than a clean decomposition.

key_findings.claim: At a matched 50-protein label budget, top-10 unweighted fusion and an L1-logistic regression over all 660 head features are statistically indistinguishable on the 29-protein CAMEO evaluation.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix reports P@L/2 of 0.4590 for fusion and 0.4565 for the truncated Rao-style L1 probe, delta +0.0025 with 95% CI [-0.005,+0.009] and p=0.49. All-head (0.1628) and late-layer (0.3032) means are much worse, showing that labeled feature selection or fitting—not averaging indiscriminately—carries the gain.

key_findings.claim: The matched-budget control is not the same end-to-end leakage-clean protocol used for the headline CAMEO result, despite language that conflates them.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix G trains both the top-10 ranking and L1 regression on Zhang-50, whereas the headline clean pipeline selects on 10 filtered CAMEO proteins. It also reports C=1 after testing C in {0.01,0.1,1.0} without naming an independent validation set. The 50-protein comparison is still label-budget matched, but its selection stage can inherit Zhang-benchmark overlap and its regularization choice may be evaluation-tuned.

anchors.section: G and Table A5, Zhang-50 matched-budget control

key_findings.claim: The stated bootstrap test is not the exchangeability randomization test suggested by its prose.
key_findings.evidence: The implementation resamples proteins with replacement and reports the fraction of bootstrap mean deltas at or below zero; it does not swap method labels within proteins under a sharp null or recenter a null bootstrap. Operator-grid p-values are unadjusted. Appendix B also says only AMPLIFY survives its Bonferroni cutoff 0.006, while Table A3 reports p<0.001 for both AMPLIFY and ESM-2-650M spectral consensus, an internal multiplicity-summary inconsistency.

key_findings.claim: Several appendix negatives bound the universality of naive top-10 fusion and the value of combining it with CJ.
key_findings.evidence: At K=10, ESM-2-8M trails logit-CJ on Zhang eval-200 (0.211 vs 0.234); naive mean is best on only 8 of 16 operator cells, with spectral consensus improving AMPLIFY by 1.82 points and ESM-2-650M by 0.64 points; and z-score ensembling CJ with fusion is flat or slightly negative across three tested cells.

method.core_idea: Read long-range residue contacts directly from the small subset of attention heads whose maps align with labeled contacts, avoiding the categorical Jacobian's exhaustive amino-acid perturbations.
method.mechanism: A disjoint labeled selection set ranks individually symmetrized and APC-corrected attention maps by long-range P@L/2. The top-K maps are averaged with equal weight. Representation-CJ is a separate perturbation baseline/extension based on hidden-state displacement; an attempted CJ-plus-fusion ensemble does not improve fusion alone.
assumptions: A small selection set identifies contact-relevant heads that transfer to a disjoint evaluation set.
Current-UniRef50 sequence similarity is a conservative proxy for pretraining overlap in older checkpoints.
Attention maps expose pair structure in a coordinate system comparable across proteins and models after symmetrization and APC.
The selected K and any operator choice must transfer from selection data; the reported cross-model sweet-K/diffuseness analysis does not fully satisfy this separation.
Long-range P@L/2 under the stated 8-angstrom contact definitions is an adequate contact-recovery metric.

techniques.role: Uses selected, symmetrized, APC-corrected attention maps as one-pass contact scores.
Ranks heads and chooses K using a small labeled protein set disjoint from evaluation.
Compares logit- and representation-level perturbation readouts.
Filters CAMEO targets by temporal cutoff and similarity to a proxy pretraining corpus.

evaluations.setting: ESM-2-650M on CAMEO-PTA25, 10 selection and 29 evaluation proteins
evaluations.result: Fusion reports 0.459 versus 0.369 for categorical Jacobian and 0.396 for top-1 attention, with p<0.001 for fusion versus CJ.
evaluations.baseline: Logit categorical Jacobian and globally selected top-1 attention head

evaluations.setting: Cross-architecture pretraining-aware protocol on ESM-2-3B, ProtT5-XL, ESM-1b, and partially clean newer models
evaluations.result: Fusion versus CJ is 0.463 versus 0.369 on ESM-2-3B (+9.4 points), 0.418 versus 0.359 on ProtT5-XL (+5.9), and 0.348 versus 0.289 on ESM-1b (+5.9), all on the same N=29 draw and reported p<0.001.
evaluations.baseline: Best available logit- or representation-CJ per architecture

evaluations.setting: Zhang eval-200 across nine protein-LM variants plus CASP14 checks
evaluations.metric: Long-range contact precision and method correlation
evaluations.result: At K=10, fusion exceeds CJ for ESM-2 at 35M-3B and ESM-1b, but loses on ESM-2-8M (0.211 vs 0.234). On ESM-2-650M/3B, repr-CJ and logit-CJ have per-protein r=0.96/0.95 and pair-score Pearson 0.946/0.930 on smaller pair-level subsamples.
evaluations.baseline: Categorical Jacobian, top-1 head, and prior attention readouts

evaluations.metric: Long-range P@L/2 for attention, representation-CJ, and fusion
evaluations.result: Top-head/repr-CJ/fusion are 0.193/0.056/0.112 for ProGen2-xlarge on Zhang eval-200 and 0.033/0.013/0.023 for ProGen2-large on Zhang-50.

evaluations.setting: Zhang-50 matched-label-budget training with evaluation on CAMEO eval-29
evaluations.metric: P@L/2 and significance of fusion-versus-L1 difference
evaluations.result: Fusion is 0.4590 versus 0.4565 for L1 regression (delta +0.0025, 95% CI [-0.005,+0.009], p=0.49); all-head and late-layer means are 0.1628 and 0.3032.
evaluations.baseline: Rao-style L1 probe, all-head mean, and late-head mean

evaluations.setting: Paired A100-80GB bf16 inference timing on Zhang eval-200
evaluations.metric: Median seconds per protein, CJ/fusion ratio, and peak GPU memory
evaluations.result: Speedup rises from 150x at ESM-2-35M (4.7/0.032 s) to 1626x at ESM-2-3B (87.3/0.054 s); peak memory is 2.4/0.5 GiB and 44.9/19.5 GiB respectively.
evaluations.baseline: Batched 19L+1-forward categorical Jacobian on the same proteins and hardware

evaluations.setting: ESM-2-650M selection-size sweep, 20 draws per size from Zhang-50 and a disjoint 50-protein holdout
evaluations.metric: Top-10-head Jaccard versus the full-50 ranking and holdout P@L/2
evaluations.result: At 10 labeled proteins, Jaccard is 0.991+/-0.040 and holdout precision 0.783+/-0.002 versus 0.782 for the full-50 ranking; this validates top-10 ranking stability for one architecture, not cross-architecture sweet-K selection.

limitations: Author-stated: CAMEO-PTA25 is small and defined by sequence rather than structure or fold novelty.
Author-stated: the current UniRef50 release is a proxy for checkpoint-era pretraining data, and cleanliness is model-relative.
Author-stated: newer ESM Cambrian and AMPLIFY models postdate the cutoff, so absolute scores are not leakage-clean.
Author-stated: causal-model evidence is limited to two ProGen2 scales, and some newer architectures are not evaluated.
Reviewer inference: head selection consumes pairwise contact labels even though no per-pair or per-head weights are fitted.
Reviewer inference: the primary N=29 sample yields limited precision for architecture-level generalization and subgroup analyses.
Reviewer inference: the bootstrap p-value is not a sharp-null randomization test, and the operator grid is mostly unadjusted for multiplicity.

Reviewer inference: the diffuseness statistic and sweet-K values are reported on Zhang eval-200 itself; numeric holdout-K transfer is omitted, so that mechanism-level selection claim remains post-hoc.
Reviewer inference: the 50-protein L1 control trains on Zhang-50 rather than the filtered CAMEO selection set and does not identify an independent set for choosing C.

Reviewer inference: the paired runtime result is hardware- and batching-specific and omits label acquisition and search, though the 19L+1-versus-one forward-count gap remains decisive after modest amortization.
failure_modes: Selecting too many diffuse or irrelevant heads dilutes a concentrated contact signal, as in the smallest ESM-2 setting.
A pretraining-aware split for one model remains contaminated for a newer checkpoint trained after the cutoff.
Causal/autoregressive pretraining fails to place symmetric pair structure in attention or perturbation responses.
Current-UniRef representatives fail to reproduce historical pretraining membership exactly.
An apparent leakage effect is inflated by simultaneous changes in protein length, benchmark difficulty, and contact definition.
Long proteins exceed the native context and require stitching, creating boundary and score-calibration artifacts.
A sweet-K or fusion operator selected on the evaluation set can overstate cross-architecture adaptability even when the fixed K=10 headline remains valid.
reusable_insights: Separate label-free scoring from label-supervised model selection; both belong in the sample and compute budget.
Evaluate mechanistic biological readouts on temporally and pretraining-aware targets before claiming de novo generalization.
A simple unweighted probe can be competitive when supervision is spent on feature selection rather than coefficient fitting.
Perturbation-derived readouts should be compared to the internal activations they reconstruct; high agreement may reveal a cheaper sufficient statistic.
Report absolute cleanliness per checkpoint, not once per benchmark, because protein corpora and model release dates differ.
Use a matched-label-budget supervised baseline to locate whether gains come from selection, aggregation, or functional form.
open_questions: Does selected-head fusion retain its margin on a larger prospective post-pretraining protein set with fold-level novelty?
Can head selection be made genuinely label-free using conservation, sparse features, or model-internal perturbation agreement?
Why do bidirectional objectives expose contacts while the tested causal objectives do not, and can a controlled pretraining comparison isolate the cause?
Does contact-head diffuseness predict other structural capabilities or only this P@L/2 readout?
Can a streaming or block-sparse implementation preserve one-pass contact recovery for proteins far beyond context length?
How much of the Zhang-to-CAMEO drop is memorization versus target difficulty under a matched benchmark design?

competitive_landscape.title: BERTology Meets Biology: Interpreting Attention in Protein Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Directly audits whether individual protein-language-model attention heads align with tertiary contacts and other biophysical annotations.
competitive_landscape.difference: It measures high-confidence attention-to-contact alignment across five earlier protein Transformers and explicitly treats the result as associative; the present paper converts selected heads into a contact-ranking method, compares against categorical Jacobians, and adds pretraining-aware filtering.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer protein language models are unsupervised structure learners
competitive_landscape.relationship: Establishes attention-map contact prediction with a supervised logistic probe over heads.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns L1-regularized head coefficients at larger label budget; this paper uses unweighted averaging after small-set supervised head and K selection and adds leakage-aware evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Single Layers of Attention Suffice to Predict Protein Contacts
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct attention-contact predecessor showing contact signal concentrated in very few ProtBERT-BFD heads and studying single-layer factored attention.
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes contact-predictive heads and develops an energy-based single-layer model rather than benchmarking a small-label top-K readout against CJ across pretrained architectures and a pretraining-aware split.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2021 EBM Workshop poster; published 2021-04-25, last modified 2023-05-05

competitive_landscape.title: MSA Transformer
competitive_landscape.relationship: Predicts contacts from row/column attention over multiple-sequence alignments with high unsupervised precision.
competitive_landscape.difference: It requires an input MSA and a model trained for aligned families; the present readout operates on single-sequence protein language models and focuses on selecting existing heads.

competitive_landscape.title: Protein language models trained on multiple sequence alignments learn phylogenetic relationships
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct attention-contact comparator studying simple MSA-Transformer attention combinations under phylogenetic noise.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses MSA row attention for unsupervised contacts and tests resilience to phylogenetic correlations; the present paper uses label-selected single-sequence attention heads and compares their cost and precision directly with categorical Jacobians.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v2 (2022-09-21), corresponding to Nature Communications 13:6298

competitive_landscape.title: Beware of Data Leakage from Protein LLM Pretraining
competitive_landscape.relationship: Provides the pretraining-aware sequence-similarity evaluation protocol adapted by this paper.
competitive_landscape.difference: It demonstrates leakage effects on thermostability prediction, whereas the present work applies a related filter to unsupervised contact recovery and compares readout mechanisms.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a one-forward-pass top-K attention alternative that matches or beats categorical Jacobians across bidirectional models, a representation-level Jacobian, and a leakage-clean primary comparison.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The distinctive empirical package combines small-set head selection, a 29-protein pretraining-aware protocol, cross-architecture replication, matched-label controls, and logit-/representation-Jacobian agreement.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Attention-based contact prediction, sparse supervised head selection, unweighted top-head averaging, single-layer contact concentration, MSA-attention contact readout, and categorical Jacobians are all prior. The credible novelty is the direct one-pass versus CJ comparison under a small labeled head-ranking budget, the model-relative CAMEO evaluation, and output-head-independent representation-CJ. Claims that the method uses no per-pair labels and that diffuseness prospectively predicts K are too strong: pair-contact labels drive selection, and the cross-model K/diffuseness association is reported on eval-200 itself.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification read all 28 pinned pages and checked Tables 1-4 and A1-A13 plus Figures 1-3 and A1-A6. The fixed-K=10 CAMEO result and paired timing numbers match the PDF. Repairs distinguish global selected top-1 from the table's inconsistent 'per-protein top-1' label, correct section/page anchors, narrow the runtime caveat, and separate the genuine matched-label null result from its Zhang-50 selection and unspecified C-validation. The bootstrap tail fraction is not the exchangeability test named in prose. Seven primary records were checked, including the PNAS categorical-Jacobian source; six version-pinned records form the structured competitor panel.

verification.passage_check: Read the pinned 28-page arXiv v2 PDF end to end, including references and Appendices A-Q. Rechecked every existing finding, evaluation, limitation, failure mode, novelty statement, and anchor against the page-marked PDF; specifically audited Tables 1-4 and A1-A13, the CAMEO 553-to-56-to-39-to-10/29 construction, 19L+1 accounting, repr/logit pair metrics, causal negatives, bootstrap procedure, operator multiplicity, matched-budget provenance, selection-size sweep, timing, and long-context stitching. Incorrect page/section anchors and the overbroad hardware caveat were repaired; post-hoc K/diffuseness and Zhang-50 control inconsistencies were added.
verification.competitor_check: Re-searched official primary literature for categorical Jacobians, protein-attention contact readouts, sparse head probes, single-layer contact models, MSA-attention contact prediction, phylogenetic robustness, and pretraining leakage. Verified the PNAS DOI 10.1073/pnas.2406285121 categorical-Jacobian version of record and six version-pinned panel records: arXiv 2006.15222v3, OpenReview fylclEqgvgd ICLR 2021 poster, OpenReview byj2AP4KRtf ICLR 2021 EBM Workshop poster, PMLR v139/rao21a, arXiv 2203.15465v2, and PMLR v261/hermann24a. The first five panel records are direct method predecessors or competitors; Hermann is the adopted evaluation-protocol comparator.
